title.en: Advanced Comparison (the more … the better, far better, by far the best)
title.es: La comparación avanzada (the more … the better, far better, by far the best)

text.en: You already know the basics: -er/more … than, as … as, the -est/the most. At B2 refinements come on top. The + comparative, the + comparative: “The more you practice, the better you get.” Strong or weak modifiers: much/far/a lot taller, slightly/a bit taller. Equality: twice as fast as, not nearly as good as. Superlatives: by far the best, the second largest, the least expensive. The Spanish “cuanto más…, mejor…”, “mucho más” and “con diferencia el mejor” match these.
text.es: Ya conoces lo básico: -er/more … than, as … as, the -est/the most. En B2 se añaden los matices. The + comparativo, the + comparativo: «The more you practice, the better you get.» Modificadores fuertes o débiles: much/far/a lot taller, slightly/a bit taller. Igualdad: twice as fast as, not nearly as good as. Superlativos: by far the best, the second largest, the least expensive. El «cuanto más…, mejor…», el «mucho más» y el «con diferencia el mejor» del español les corresponden.

text.en: Two parallel comparatives say that one change causes another. A short form: “The sooner, the better.”
text.es: Dos comparativos paralelos dicen que un cambio provoca otro. Una forma corta: «The sooner, the better.»

title.en: Modifiers: much, far, a lot, slightly, a bit
title.es: Modificadores: much, far, a lot, slightly, a bit

text.en: A big difference: much, far, a lot, considerably + comparative. A small difference: slightly, a bit, a little. Very cannot be used before a comparative: not “very taller”.
text.es: Una gran diferencia: much, far, a lot, considerably + comparativo. Una diferencia pequeña: slightly, a bit, a little. Very no se puede usar antes de un comparativo: no «very taller».

examples.es: This phone is much more expensive than that one.

tr.en: This phone is much more expensive than that one.
tr.es: Este celular es mucho más caro que aquel.

examples.es: She is slightly taller than her sister.

tr.en: She is slightly taller than her sister.
tr.es: Ella es un poco más alta que su hermana.

title.en: Equality: as … as, the same as, different from
title.es: Igualdad: as … as, the same as, different from

text.en: Between as … as goes an adjective: as tall as. With countable nouns as many, with uncountable nouns as much. After “the same” comes as, after “different” comes from.
text.es: Entre as … as va un adjetivo: as tall as. Con sustantivos contables as many, con incontables as much. Después de «the same» va as, después de «different» va from.

examples.es: He runs twice as fast as I do.

tr.en: He runs twice as fast as I do.
tr.es: Corre el doble de rápido que yo.

examples.es: My car is the same as yours.

tr.en: My car is the same as yours.
tr.es: Mi carro es igual que el tuyo.

text.en: Not nearly as … as means much less so: “It is not nearly as good as the old one.”
text.es: Not nearly as … as significa mucho menos: «It is not nearly as good as the old one.»

examples.es: It is not nearly as good as the old one.

tr.en: It is not nearly as good as the old one.
tr.es: No es ni de cerca tan bueno como el anterior.

tr.en: I have as many books as you.

title.en: Superlatives refined: by far, second, least
title.es: Superlativos matizados: by far, second, least

text.en: By far stresses a big gap: by far the best. An ordinal: the second largest. For little the least + adjective: the least expensive. After one of the comes a plural. Easily also stresses: easily the best.
text.es: By far resalta una gran diferencia: by far the best. Un ordinal: the second largest. Para lo menos the least + adjetivo: the least expensive. Después de one of the va un plural. Easily también refuerza: easily the best.

examples.es: It is by far the best hotel in town.

tr.en: It is by far the best hotel in town.
tr.es: Es, con diferencia, el mejor hotel de la ciudad.

examples.es: He is one of the best players in the world.

tr.en: He is one of the best players in the world.
tr.es: Es uno de los mejores jugadores del mundo.

title.en: A continuing change: colder and colder
title.es: Un cambio continuo: colder and colder

text.en: Repeating the comparative says the change keeps growing. With long adjectives use more and more: “more and more expensive”.
text.es: Repetir el comparativo dice que el cambio sigue creciendo. Con adjetivos largos se usa more and more: «more and more expensive».

tr.en: It's getting colder and colder.
tr.es: Cada vez hace más frío.

examples.es: Life is getting more and more expensive.

tr.en: Life is getting more and more expensive.
tr.es: La vida se está poniendo cada vez más cara.

text.en: The Spanish “mejor que” is better than in English, not “more good than”. After “the same” comes as: not “the same than” and not “the same like”.
text.es: El «mejor que» del español es better than en inglés, no «more good than». Después de «the same» va as: no «the same than» ni «the same like».

text.en: The Spanish “igual de … que” is as … as in English: “as tall as”. The Spanish “el doble de … que” is twice as … as: “twice as fast as”.
text.es: El «igual de … que» del español es as … as en inglés: «as tall as». El «el doble de … que» es twice as … as: «twice as fast as».

speak.en: At the advanced level, comparison gets refinements. The «the more you practice, the better you get» structure uses two parallel comparatives. Strong modifiers are «much», «far» and «a lot», weak ones are «slightly» and «a bit». «Very» cannot stand before a comparative. Equality: «twice as fast as». After «the same» comes «as», after «different» comes «from». Superlatives: «by far the best» and «the second largest». A continuing change: «colder and colder».
speak.es: En el nivel avanzado la comparación recibe matices. La estructura «the more you practice, the better you get» usa dos comparativos paralelos. Los modificadores fuertes son «much», «far» y «a lot», los débiles son «slightly» y «a bit». «Very» no puede ir antes de un comparativo. Igualdad: «twice as fast as». Después de «the same» va «as», después de «different» va «from». Superlativos: «by far the best» y «the second largest». Un cambio continuo: «colder and colder».

items.sentence: The more you practice, the ___ you get.

why.en: The partner of the + comparative is the + comparative: the better.
why.es: La pareja de the + comparativo es the + comparativo: the better.

best.en: The best is a superlative; the “the more …, the …” structure needs a comparative.
best.es: The best es un superlativo; la estructura «the more …, the …» pide un comparativo.

well.en: Well is an adverb in the base form; after the you need the comparative (better).
well.es: Well es un adverbio en grado base; después de the hace falta el comparativo (better).

examples: The harder you try, the better.
The older he gets, the wiser he is.

tr.en: The more you practice, the better you get.
tr.es: Mientras más practiques, mejor te volverás.

items.sentence: The ___ you leave, the earlier you arrive.

why.en: A comparative after the: the sooner.
why.es: Un comparativo después de the: the sooner.

soon.en: Soon is the base form; the “the … the” structure needs the comparative (sooner).
soon.es: Soon es el grado base; la estructura «the … the» pide el comparativo (sooner).

soonest.en: Soonest is a superlative; the structure needs a comparative.
soonest.es: Soonest es un superlativo; la estructura pide un comparativo.

examples: The sooner, the better.
The earlier you go, the better.

tr.en: The sooner you leave, the earlier you arrive.
tr.es: Cuanto antes te vayas, más temprano llegarás.

items.sentence: This phone is ___ more expensive than that one.

why.en: A strong modifier before a comparative: much more expensive.
why.es: Un modificador fuerte antes de un comparativo: much more expensive.

very.en: Very cannot stand before a comparative.
very.es: Very no puede ir antes de un comparativo.

most.en: Most marks a superlative; than asks for a comparative.
most.es: Most marca un superlativo; than pide un comparativo.

examples: This is much better.
He is much taller.

tr.en: This phone is much more expensive than that one.
tr.es: Este celular es mucho más caro que ese.

items.sentence: She is ___ taller than her sister.

why.en: A weak modifier before a comparative: slightly taller.
why.es: Un modificador débil antes de un comparativo: slightly taller.

very.en: Very cannot stand before a comparative.
very.es: Very no puede ir antes de un comparativo.

most.en: Most marks a superlative; than asks for a comparative.
most.es: Most marca un superlativo; than pide un comparativo.

examples: He is slightly older.
It is slightly warmer.

tr.en: She is slightly taller than her sister.
tr.es: Ella es un poco más alta que su hermana.

items.sentence: She is ___ as tall as her brother.

why.es: Enfatizar la igualdad: just as … as.

very.en: “Very as tall as” is not correct; just or nearly fits before as … as.
very.es: «Very as tall as» no es correcto; antes de as … as encaja just o nearly.

more.en: “More as tall as” is not correct; as … as is not mixed with more.
more.es: «More as tall as» no es correcto; as … as no se mezcla con more.

examples: He is just as old as me.
It is just as big as that.

tr.en: She is just as tall as her brother.
tr.es: Ella es exactamente tan alta como su hermano.

items.sentence: He runs ___ as fast as I do.

why.en: For a multiple: twice as fast as.
why.es: Para un múltiplo: twice as fast as.

double.en: “Double as fast as” is not correct; twice or three times goes before as … as.
double.es: «Double as fast as» no es correcto; antes de as … as va twice o three times.

two.en: “Two as fast as” is not correct; a double ratio needs twice.
two.es: «Two as fast as» no es correcto; una proporción doble necesita twice.

examples: She runs twice as far.
It is twice as big as mine.

tr.en: He runs twice as fast as I do.
tr.es: Él corre el doble de rápido que yo.

items.sentence: This is the ___ expensive hotel in town.

why.en: A superlative for little: the least + adjective.
why.es: Un superlativo para lo menos: the least + adjetivo.

little.en: Little is not a superlative; after the you need the least.
little.es: Little no es un superlativo; después de the hace falta the least.

fewest.en: Fewest goes with countable nouns; before an adjective you need the least.
fewest.es: Fewest va con sustantivos contables; antes de un adjetivo hace falta the least.

examples: It is the least useful.
She is the least tired.

tr.en: This is the least expensive hotel in town.
tr.es: Este es el hotel menos caro de la ciudad.

items.sentence: She is ___ the best player in the team.

why.en: Stressing a big gap: by far the best.
why.es: Resaltar una gran diferencia: by far the best.

far by.en: “Far by” does not exist; the order is by far.
far by.es: «Far by» no existe; el orden es by far.

much by.en: “Much by” does not exist in this structure; you need by far.
much by.es: «Much by» no existe en esta estructura; hace falta by far.

examples: It is by far the biggest.
He is by far the fastest.

tr.en: She is by far the best player in the team.
tr.es: Ella es por mucho la mejor jugadora del equipo.

why.en: A continuing change: the comparative repeated with and, colder and colder.
why.es: Un cambio continuo: el comparativo repetido con and, colder and colder.

or.en: “Colder or colder” does not express a continuing change; you need and.
or.es: «Colder or colder» no expresa un cambio continuo; hace falta and.

than.en: “Colder than colder” makes no sense; a continuing change needs and.
than.es: «Colder than colder» no tiene sentido; un cambio continuo necesita and.

examples: It is getting darker and darker.
She runs faster and faster.

tr.en: It's getting colder and colder.
tr.es: Cada vez hace más frío.

items.sentence: It is ___ the best restaurant in town.

why.en: Strengthening a superlative with an adverb: easily the best.
why.es: Reforzar un superlativo con un adverbio: easily the best.

easy.en: Easy is an adjective; before a superlative you need an adverb (easily).
easy.es: Easy es un adjetivo; antes de un superlativo hace falta un adverbio (easily).

ease.en: Ease is a noun or a verb; before a superlative you need an adverb (easily).
ease.es: Ease es un sustantivo o un verbo; antes de un superlativo hace falta un adverbio (easily).

examples: She is easily the fastest.
This is easily the worst.

tr.en: It is easily the best restaurant in town.
tr.es: Es por mucho el mejor restaurante de la ciudad.

items.sentence: My car is the same ___ yours.

why.es: Después de the same va as.

than.en: “The same than” is a mistake carried over from Spanish; you need as.
than.es: «The same than» es un error que viene del español; hace falta as.

like.en: “The same like” is a mistake carried over from Spanish; you need as.
like.es: «The same like» es un error que viene del español; hace falta as.

examples: It is the same as mine.
She has the same bag as me.

tr.en: My car is the same as yours.
tr.es: Mi carro es igual al tuyo.

as.en: “Different as” is not correct; you need from.
as.es: «Different as» no es correcto; hace falta from.

of.en: “Different of” is not correct; you need from.
of.es: «Different of» no es correcto; hace falta from.

examples: This is different from that.
She is different from him.

tr.en: Her accent is different from mine.
tr.es: Su acento es diferente al mío.

items.sentence: I have as ___ books as you.

why.en: A countable noun between as … as: as many.
why.es: Un sustantivo contable entre as … as: as many.

much.en: As much goes with uncountable nouns; books is countable.
much.es: As much va con sustantivos incontables; books es contable.

more.en: “As more” does not belong to the as … as structure.
more.es: «As more» no pertenece a la estructura as … as.

examples: She has as many friends as me.
I read as many as you.

tr.en: I have as many books as you.
tr.es: Tengo tantos libros como tú.

items.sentence: I have as ___ money as you.

why.en: An uncountable noun between as … as: as much.
why.es: Un sustantivo incontable entre as … as: as much.

many.en: As many goes with countable nouns; money is uncountable.
many.es: As many va con sustantivos contables; money es incontable.

more.en: “As more” does not belong to the as … as structure.
more.es: «As more» no pertenece a la estructura as … as.

examples: He has as much time as me.
We need as much as you.

tr.en: I have as much money as you.
tr.es: Tengo tanto dinero como tú.

items.sentence: The ___ you worry, the better you sleep.

why.en: The “the … the” structure takes a comparative: the less.
why.es: La estructura «the … the» lleva un comparativo: the less.

least.en: Least is a superlative; the “the … the” structure needs a comparative (less).
least.es: Least es un superlativo; la estructura «the … the» pide un comparativo (less).

lesser.en: Lesser does not replace less for quantity; you need less.
lesser.es: Lesser no reemplaza a less para cantidad; hace falta less.

examples: The less you spend, the more you save.
The less he talks, the better.

tr.en: The less you worry, the better you sleep.
tr.es: Mientras menos te preocupes, mejor duermes.

items.sentence: He is one of the ___ players in the world.

why.en: After one of the comes a superlative and a plural: the best players.
why.es: Después de one of the va un superlativo y un plural: the best players.

better.en: Better is a comparative; after one of the you need a superlative.
better.es: Better es un comparativo; después de one of the hace falta un superlativo.

good.en: Good is the base form; after one of the you need a superlative.
good.es: Good es el grado base; después de one of the hace falta un superlativo.

examples: She is one of the smartest.
It is one of the biggest.

tr.en: He is one of the best players in the world.
tr.es: Él es uno de los mejores jugadores del mundo.

items.sentence: The harder you work, the ___ you will be.

why.en: The comparative of a long adjective after the: the more successful.
why.es: El comparativo de un adjetivo largo después de the: the more successful.

most successful.en: Most successful is a superlative; the “the … the” structure needs a comparative.
most successful.es: Most successful es un superlativo; la estructura «the … the» pide un comparativo.

successful more.en: The order of “successful more” is reversed; you need more successful.
successful more.es: El orden de «successful more» está invertido; hace falta more successful.

examples: The more careful you are, the better.
The more you read, the more you know.

tr.en: The harder you work, the more successful you will be.
tr.es: Mientras más duro trabajes, más éxito tendrás.
